question: What is the primary purpose of the Basel Convention?

options.A: To establish universal standards for hospital design
options.B: To fund renewable energy projects globally
options.C: To eliminate all forms of municipal garbage
options.D: To regulate international transport of hazardous wastes

explanation: The treaty focuses specifically on controlling and minimizing the cross-border movement of hazardous materials to protect vulnerable regions. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h1)

question: Why did developing nations experience a surge of toxic waste dumping prior to 1989?

options.A: Developing countries actively requested toxic materials for industry
options.B: Stringent environmental laws at home made disposal expensive
options.C: Developed nations lacked any domestic storage facilities
options.D: Global shipping costs dropped to zero for chemical loads

explanation: Stricter regulations and high disposal costs in industrialized countries drove entities to seek cheap, unregulated dumping grounds abroad. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h1)

question: What does the proximity principle dictate regarding waste management?

options.A: Incineration plants must be built near capital cities only
options.B: Waste must be disposed of as close to its generation point as possible
options.C: All toxic materials must be shipped to remote uninhabited islands
options.D: Storage sites should be located at least 500 kilometers from borders

explanation: The proximity principle aims to minimize the environmental and safety risks associated with long-distance transport of dangerous substances. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h2)

question: The concept of self-sufficiency under the convention encourages countries to do which of the following?

options.B: Handle their generated waste within their own borders
options.C: Export all industrial byproducts to reduce local footprint
options.D: Rely entirely on international aid for waste processing

explanation: Self-sufficiency places the responsibility of waste management back onto the nation that produced the waste in the first place. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h2)

question: Which characteristic is used to classify a substance as hazardous under the treaty?
explanation: Hazardous classifications are based on dangerous properties like being flammable, toxic, explosive, or corrosive. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h3)

question: How are hazardous materials often illegally disguised during cross-border shipping attempts?
explanation: Traders frequently mislabel toxic refuse as recyclable raw materials to evade strict customs inspections and regulatory bans. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h3)

question: What is the primary requirement of the Prior Informed Consent procedure?

options.A: Public advertisement of the waste cargo in international newspapers
options.B: Payment of a carbon tax prior to vessel departure
options.C: Written authorization from the importing country before shipment
options.D: Verbal agreement between shipping captains over maritime radio

explanation: The PIC procedure ensures no hazardous cargo crosses a border without explicit, documented consent from the receiving nation. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h4)

question: A chemical company in Europe wants to export industrial solvent waste to an African nation. What must occur before the cargo ships?

options.A: The European Union parliament must review the chemical formula
options.B: The receiving nation must formally evaluate and consent to the shipment in writing
options.C: Local residents near the destination port must vote on the cargo acceptance
options.D: The shipping company must pay a disposal fee directly to the United Nations

explanation: Under the PIC mechanism, legal transport requires advance notification and explicit written approval from the destination country. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h4)

question: What is a primary environmental consequence of improper hazardous waste disposal in developing regions?

options.A: Rapid expansion of arable agricultural land
options.B: Contamination of local water tables and aquifers
options.D: Immediate cooling of local atmospheric temperatures

explanation: Leaching toxic substances easily penetrate soil layers, polluting vital underground water sources used for drinking and irrigation. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h5)

question: Which health hazard is directly linked to exposure from improperly handled electronic waste?

options.A: Heavy metal toxicity from lead and mercury
options.B: Acute vitamin deficiencies from dietary absorption
options.C: Bacterial infections similar to cholera outbreaks
options.D: Skeletal fractures due to sudden bone softening

explanation: Discarded electronics contain hazardous elements like lead, mercury, and cadmium that pose severe toxicity risks upon improper breakdown. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h5)

question: How does the core philosophy of international waste treaties translate into daily clinical nursing duties?

options.A: By mandating that nurses personally transport waste to municipal incinerators
options.B: By guiding rigorous bedside segregation of infectious and hazardous materials
options.C: By shifting all responsibility for chemical safety onto hospital pharmacists
options.D: By requiring nurses to negotiate international trade agreements

explanation: High-level environmental principles rely on baseline clinical practices like proper segregation to ensure safe, responsible waste handling. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical category of hazardous waste generated within a standard healthcare facility?
explanation: Agricultural crops are produced on farms, whereas healthcare facilities generate sharps, pharmaceuticals, and biological specimens. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h6)
